title: One-degree extension of a presentable partial subcomplex with controlled cohomology image
statement: Fix a universe $U$ for small sets and Hom sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B$ be full replete, contain zero, and be closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions in $\mathcal B$. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian with the induced exact structure and is closed under $U$-small ambient coproducts. For an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in U$, call a small category $\lambda$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; write $\mathcal C^\lambda$ for these objects in a category $\mathcal C$. Regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. Fix an uncountable regular $\lambda$ with the following properties. Put $\mathcal S=\mathcal B^\lambda$. Assume $\mathcal S$ is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in $\mathcal B$; every object of $\mathcal A$ is an ambient $U$-small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of subobjects in $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$; and every pair $x\twoheadrightarrow y\leftarrow n$ in $\mathcal B$, with $n\in\mathcal S$, has a commutative lift $x\leftarrow m\twoheadrightarrow n$ with $m\in\mathcal S$, chosen monic into $x$ when $n\to y$ is monic. Let $Z^\bullet$ be an unbounded cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $H^j(Z)\in\mathcal A$ for every integer $j$. Let $i\le b$ be integers and let $N^j\subseteq Z^j$ for $i\le j\le b$, with $N^j=0$ for $j>b$, be a partial subcomplex: $d_Z(N^j)\subseteq N^{j+1}$. Assume every $N^j\in\mathcal S$, its cohomology in each degree $j>i$ belongs to $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$, and the image of $K^i=\ker(N^i\to N^{i+1})\to H^i(Z)$ belongs to $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$. There is a subobject $N^{i-1}\subseteq Z^{i-1}$ in $\mathcal S$ with $d_Z(N^{i-1})\subseteq N^i$ such that the extended partial subcomplex has cohomology in $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$ in every degree $j>i-1$, and the image of $\ker(N^{i-1}\to N^i)\to H^{i-1}(Z)$ belongs to $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$. All previously chosen terms and differentials are retained.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, downward induction after conditions (1)--(3), from the pullback defining L^i through the final epimorphism lift; the final N^i is read as N^{i-1} Hall--Neeman--Rydh, arXiv:1405.1888, Appendix A. No Stacks tag states this input; archive WANTED, online source read.

proof.text: Write $Y^j=\ker d_Z^j$, $X^j=\operatorname{im}d_Z^{j-1}$ and $H^j=Y^j/X^j$. The partial-subcomplex condition embeds $K=\ker(N^i\to N^{i+1})$ in $Y^i$. Put $L=K\times_{Y^i}X^i$, its intersection with the boundaries. Thus $L$ is the kernel of $K\to H^i$, and both $K$ and $L$ lie in $\mathcal S$ by its assumed closure under subobjects of $N^i$. Put $J=\operatorname{im}(K\to H^i)$; the hypothesis says $J\in\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, pullback defining $L^i$ after induction conditions (1)--(3)

proof.text: Put $E=Z^{i-1}/X^{i-1}$. The differential induces an epimorphism $e:E\twoheadrightarrow X^i$ with kernel $H^{i-1}\hookrightarrow E$: its kernel is $Y^{i-1}/X^{i-1}$. Indeed an element of $E$ lifts after an epimorphic refinement to $Z^{i-1}$; it is killed by $e$ exactly when that lift is a cycle. Apply the assumed small epimorphism-lift property to $E\twoheadrightarrow X^i\leftarrow L$. Since $L\hookrightarrow X^i$ is monic, obtain a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow E$ with $M\in\mathcal S$ and an epimorphism $v:M\twoheadrightarrow L$. Let $T=\ker v$. Then $T=M\times_E H^{i-1}$: both conditions say that the composite to $X^i$ vanishes. In particular $T\in\mathcal S$, and $T\to H^{i-1}$ is monic since $M\to E$ is monic.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, first small lift $M^i$ and pullback $\widetilde M^i$; the kernel calculation is written out using epimorphic refinements

proof.text: Use the given ambient small $\lambda$-filtered presentation $H^{i-1}=\operatorname{colim}_a P_a$ by subobjects $P_a\in\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$. Presentability of $T$ says that $\operatorname{colim}_a\operatorname{Hom}(T,P_a)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,H^{i-1})$ is bijective. An element of a colimit of sets is represented by an element at one stage (the colimit is the quotient of the disjoint union). Consequently $T\hookrightarrow H^{i-1}$ factors through some $P=P_a\hookrightarrow H^{i-1}$. The map $T\to P$ is monic because its composite with $P\hookrightarrow H^{i-1}$ is monic. No preservation of arbitrary subobjects by $\mathcal A$ is asserted.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, factorization of $\widetilde M^i	o H^{i-1}(Z)$ through $P^i$

proof.text: Form the ambient pushout $Q=M\amalg_T P$. The sequence $0\to T\to M\xrightarrow{v}L\to0$ is short exact: $T$ is its kernel and $v$ is epic. The pushout-of-an-extension lemma gives a short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{\phi}L\to0$, with $\phi|_M=v$ and $\phi a=0$. Since $P,L\in\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal S$ is closed under extensions, $Q\in\mathcal S$. The maps $M\to E$ and $P\to H^{i-1}\to E$ agree on $T$, so the pushout property gives $q:Q\to E$ with $e q=(L\hookrightarrow X^i)\phi$.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, pushout defining $Q^i$; exactness supplied by Stacks Tag 010I section-extensions, pushout of extensions, via the cited node

proof.text: The map $q:Q\to E$ is monic. To check this, let $z:W\to Q$ satisfy $qz=0$. Since $L\hookrightarrow X^i$ is monic, the identity $eq=(L\hookrightarrow X^i)\phi$ implies $\phi z=0$. Exactness of $0\to P\xrightarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{\phi}L\to0$ factors $z=at$. Then $0=qz=(P\hookrightarrow H^{i-1}\hookrightarrow E)t$ implies $t=0$ and $z=0$. In a preadditive category this zero-kernel test implies monicity by applying it to the difference of any two maps. This also verifies that $\ker\phi$ maps isomorphically onto the chosen subobject $P$ of $H^{i-1}$.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, assertion about $\ker\phi$; monicity of the induced map into $Z^{i-1}/X^{i-1}$ is checked explicitly

proof.text: Apply the assumed small lift to $Z^{i-1}\twoheadrightarrow E\leftarrow Q$. Step 5 makes the right-hand map monic, so the lift supplies a subobject $N=N^{i-1}\hookrightarrow Z^{i-1}$ in $\mathcal S$ and an epimorphism $u:N\twoheadrightarrow Q$ over $E$. Its differential into $Z^i$ is the composite $N\xrightarrow{u}Q\xrightarrow{\phi}L\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow N^i\hookrightarrow Z^i$. Hence it lands in the retained term $N^i$, its image there is exactly $L$ (both $u$ and $\phi$ are epic), and its composite with the retained outgoing differential is zero.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, final epimorphism lift; the printed final $N^i$ means $N^{i-1}$

proof.text: Let $K_{\mathrm{new}}=\ker(N\to N^i)=\ker(\phi u)$. Its map to $Q$ factors through $\ker\phi=a(P)$, giving $w:K_{\mathrm{new}}\to P$. This map is epic: for every $p:W\to P$, apply epimorphic refinements to the epic $u$ and $ap:W\to Q$, obtaining $\rho:W\prime\twoheadrightarrow W$ and $n:W\prime\to N$ with $un=ap\rho$. Then $\phi un=0$, so $n$ factors through $K_{\mathrm{new}}$ and its image under $w$ is $p\rho$, since $a$ is monic. The refinement criterion proves the assertion. The natural map $K_{\mathrm{new}}\to H^{i-1}(Z)$ is $w$ followed by $P\hookrightarrow H^{i-1}(Z)$, by the square over $E$. Its image is therefore exactly $P\in\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, omitted verification of induction condition (3) for the extended complex

proof.text: The new degree-$i$ cohomology is $K/L$, since the incoming image is $L$ by step 6. This quotient is canonically $J$: the epic map $K\twoheadrightarrow J$ has kernel $L$, and an epimorphism in an abelian category is the cokernel of its kernel. For completeness, write it as a cokernel of some $h$ by normality of epimorphisms; $h$ factors through $L$, so a map killing $L$ kills $h$ and factors uniquely through $J$. Thus the quotient universal property gives $K/L\cong J\in\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$. Cohomology in degrees $j>i$ uses only previously retained terms and differentials and is unchanged. Together with step 7 and $N\in\mathcal S$, this proves all required clauses. No term above $i-1$ was altered.

source.place: Theorem A.3 proof, omitted verification of induction conditions (1) and (2) after adjoining $N^{i-1}$

Step 7 shows the cycle map onto P is epic via lem-sp-abelian-refinements (a), so the image in H^{i-1} is P. Step 8 gives new H^i = K/L ≅ J; degrees j>i are unchanged. I re-derived every identity, and checked the edge cases i=b, L=0, T=0, P=0 and nonzero T; no boundedness below is used and no subobject closure of A is assumed.
